stemMd: What are the horizontal-axis intercepts of the ellipse x²/16 + y²/9 = 1?
explanationMd: Set y = 0 to find horizontal intercepts. Then x²/16 = 1, so x = ±4. Keeping both square roots gives the two intercepts.

distractorRationale.b: The denominator is the square of the semiaxis.
distractorRationale.a: These are vertical-axis locations, not horizontal intercepts.
distractorRationale.e: The ellipse is symmetric about the vertical axis and has two horizontal intercepts.
